content: Remember that you are an actor in a drama, of such a kind as the author pleases to make it. If short, of a short one; if long, of a long one.
author: Epictetus
story:
This insight touches directly on the messy reality of human nature. Reminding yourself of your mortality is not morbid; it is the most clarifying lens available to human consciousness. When you remember that your days are strictly numbered, petty resentments and trivial anxieties evaporate.

Across his life and work, Epictetus saw how easily we surrender our tranquility to fear, vanity, and distraction. Death gives urgency and sweetness to every ordinary afternoon. Because this day will never come again, the way you spend your attention right now is of monumental significance.
reflectionPrompt: What long-held assumption about your life or abilities is challenged by this insight?

practicalInsight: When you feel overwhelmed by minor irritations today, pause and remind yourself: 'In the grand arc of my finite life, will this matter at all?'
originalQuote: Remember that you are an actor in a play, and that the play is not yours, but the author's. If the play is short, do not complain that it is short; if it is long, do not complain that it is long.
